newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: M. Hill suffers poor sales in December.
newsitem.headline: M. Hill suffers poor sales in December.

text.p: Michael Hill International Ltd suffered poor sales in December but had performed well before and since then, MHI executives said on Tuesday.

New Zealand Managing Director Howard Bretherton said the poor December came largely down to a marketing error, when the November sales period was run into December, affecting revenue and gross profits over that period.
"We had a bad December. Everything was going sweetly and continues to run sweetly except for December, which was rotten," Bretherton told a news conference.

"We were a million dollars down on our forecasts and I think I made a couple of marketing mistakes, which won't be repeated. We brought November into December, cannibalised some of December sales and also affected our gross profit there."
MHI earlier reported a net profit of NZ$4.37 million in the six months to December from $4.13 million a year earlier, and raised the interim dividend to 3.5 cents per share from 3.0.
The company expects the full year profit to come in at between NZ$5.3 and $5.5 million against $5.32 million in the year to June, 1996.
Chairman Michael Hill said MHI would continue consolidating its position, particularly in the parts of Australia that expanded rapidly.
Hill said he expected manufacturing to become a bigger part of the company after forming a strong base. MHI also intended to become involved in jewellery repair.
"I think the manufacturing arms in both New Zealand and Australia are going to be pretty sound contributors to the success of our company in the future," he said.
MHI revamped its stores, moving away from the discount jeweller image to the mid to upper end of the market, which had paid off in the form of higher average sale returns.
"At the moment we are looking for controlled profitable growth. In difficult times like this there is no point in doing anything extreme," Hill said.
